Lookup Behavior

Lookup Behavior provides an authoritative extension point that enables identifier-based entity lookup within a FeatureCell. This behavior coordinates lookup resolution, lookup-miss resolution, and concurrent lookup fan-out through the FeatureCell state pipeline.

Lookup behavior integrates directly with state resolution and finalization. Resolved entities are populated exclusively from finalized state emissions and reconciled through controlled pipeline execution.

This behavior does not introduce time-based expiration or refresh semantics. It augments a FeatureCell with a deterministic lookup surface while preserving a single, authoritative source of truth.

Lookup Extension

When enabled, the Lookup Behavior extends the FeatureCell API with lookup methods that resolve entities by identifier. Lookup requests are coordinated through the FeatureCell pipeline and respect lifecycle boundaries, error handling, and state finalization.

Resolved entities are recorded only from finalized state emissions. When a lookup target does not exist or is removed during pipeline evaluation, resolution completes with undefined.

Lookup behavior operates as an authoritative extension. It does not mutate state directly and does not bypass pipeline execution. Instead, it reacts to committed state snapshots and augments the FeatureCell with deterministic identifier-based resolution.

Fluent Configuration

Lookup behavior is registered using the FeatureCell fluent API. Configuration is declared explicitly during FeatureCell initialization using withLookup() and is consumed during FeatureCell activation.

Notes
  • No time-based expiration is applied. Unlike cache behavior, lookup entries do not expire automatically. Recorded entities remain available until they are explicitly removed through pipeline finalization, reset, or destroy.
  • Lookup APIs and state update APIs coexist. The FeatureCell continues to expose replaceState() and mergeState() alongside lookup() and lookup$(). Direct state updates remain valid and may populate or update lookup entries when identifiers match.
  • Concurrent lookups are fan-out coordinated. Multiple lookups for the same identifier share a single in-flight pipeline resolution. All awaiting callers resolve together when finalization completes.
  • Interceptors influence lookup resolution timing. Lookup resolution occurs through the FeatureCell pipeline. Interceptors such as debounce, delay, throttling, or conditional gating may delay or suppress resolution execution.
  • Filters may intentionally discard resolved entities. FeatureCell filters may remove or suppress a resolved entity during pipeline evaluation, resulting in a finalized undefined value even when the entity exists upstream or on a remote source.
  • Lifecycle alignment is preserved. Lookup state is reset or destroyed in coordination with the owning FeatureCell lifecycle, ensuring that resolved entities never outlive the FeatureCell that produced them.
Design Decisions

Lookup behavior is designed to integrate deterministically with the FeatureCell pipeline while preserving immutability guarantees, explicit lifecycle control, and predictable resolution semantics.

Lookup Behavior Design Decisions
Condition Behavior
No Lookup Entry When no entity exists for the requested identifier, a lookup resolution is triggered through the FeatureCell pipeline using the configured fetch strategy. Resolution completes after state finalization.
Lookup Hit When a resolved entity exists in lookup state for the requested identifier, the resolved entity is returned immediately without triggering pipeline execution.
Undefined Resolution When a finalized state emission resolves to undefined for a specific identifier, the corresponding lookup entry is removed and pending lookups resolve as undefined.
Null Resolution (State Clear) A finalized state emission with a null value is treated as an authoritative state clear. All lookup entries are removed and all pending lookups resolve as undefined.
Concurrent Lookups Multiple concurrent lookups for the same identifier are coordinated through a shared pending resolution. Only one pipeline execution occurs; all awaiting callers resolve together.
replaceState / mergeState Updates State updates applied through replaceState() or mergeState() populate or update lookup entries when identifiers match.
FeatureCell Reset A FeatureCell reset clears all lookup entries and resolves all pending lookups as undefined.
FeatureCell Destroy When the owning FeatureCell is destroyed, all lookup state is cleared and all pending lookups resolve as undefined.
Pipeline Error (Scoped) When an error is finalized for a specific identifier, the corresponding lookup entry is removed and pending lookups resolve as undefined.
Pipeline Error (Global) When an error is finalized without an identifier scope, all pending lookups resolve as undefined. Lookup entries remain subject to subsequent state emissions.
Lookup Diagram
Lookup API

When lookup behavior is enabled, the FeatureCell runtime surface is extended with dedicated lookup methods.

  • lookup(id) — resolves an entity by identifier and returns a Promise that completes when resolution finalizes.
  • lookup$(id) — resolves an entity by identifier and returns an Observable that emits once and completes.

Both lookup methods coordinate lookup hits, misses, and concurrent requests through the FeatureCell pipeline. Pending lookups for the same identifier are fan-out coordinated and resolved together.

If pipeline finalization does not produce an entity for the requested identifier (for example: filtered output or scoped error finalization), lookup resolution completes with undefined.

Configuration

Enables identifier-based entity lookup for a FeatureCell. Resolved entities are indexed by a configured identifier key and populated from authoritative state emissions.

FeatureCell Initialization

The Lookup Behavior exposes a fluent configuration API that allows engineers to register lookup options during FeatureCell initialization.

This API does not perform lookup resolution directly. It records configuration that is later consumed by the Lookup Behavior during FeatureCell activation.

Fluent Lookup Configuration
Fluent API Description

withLookup(options)

input:

  • options: LookupBehaviorOptions<T>

returns: FeatureCellBaseShape (chainable)

Registers lookup configuration for a FeatureCell. The supplied options define entity identification and lookup resolution strategy.

This method must be called before initialize(). Multiple calls overwrite prior configuration.

Usage
Lookup APIs
API Description

lookup(id: string)

inputs:

  • id: string

returns:

  • Promise<TEntity>

Performs an identifier-based lookup for the specified entity. If the entity has already been resolved and recorded, the resolved value is returned immediately.

If no resolved entity exists, the lookup triggers a resolution through the FeatureCell state pipeline using the configured fetch strategy. The returned promise resolves when pipeline finalization completes. If finalization does not produce an entity, the promise resolves with undefined.

Concurrent lookups for the same identifier are automatically coordinated. Only a single pipeline resolution is executed, and all pending callers are resolved together.

lookup$(id: string)

inputs:

  • id: string

returns:

  • Observable<TEntity>

Reactive variant of lookup. Emits the resolved entity (or undefined when pipeline finalization produces no entity) and then completes.

This API integrates lookup resolution into reactive workflows while preserving the same pipeline execution, pending coordination, and fan-out semantics as the promise-based variant.

The observable emits exactly once per invocation and then completes.

Lookup Examples

Example 1: Configure Lookup Behavior

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[][]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[][]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Assumes withLookupBehavior is registered during FeatureCell setup (provideFeatureCell)
    this.vault
      .withLookup({
        idKey: 'id',
        fetchType: ResolveType.Promise,
        fetch: (id) => fetchEmployeeById(id)
      })
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    withLookupBehavior
  ]
);

// Executed during application startup (e.g. app.config.ts)
employeeCell
  .withLookup({
    idKey: 'id',
    fetchType: ResolveType.Promise,
    fetch: (id) => fetchEmployeeById(id)
  })
  .initialize();`}}

Example 2: Lookup an Entity

{{`// Promise-based lookup
const employee = await this.vault.lookup('123');

// Observable-based lookup
this.vault.lookup$('123').subscribe(emp => {
  console.info(emp);
});`}}
 
{{`// Promise-based lookup
const employee = await employeeCell.lookup('123');

// Observable-based lookup
employeeCell.lookup$('123').subscribe(emp => {
  console.info(emp);
});`}}
